behavior.setup: A project with skills.config.json, the user's registry has lead and adversary approved for two lineages; ask to grill a small feature.
behavior.prompt: /supermodo:grill add a --dry-run flag to the import command
assert: The first action is `broker.ts plan --skill grill` — before any planner brief is written
The transcript contains no `codex exec`, `claude -p` or `agy` command composed by the skill
Both planner dispatches (plan-a, plan-b) go out in the same turn, blind to each other
Question labels use the seated models' registry ids (e.g. `astra counters:`), never `Claude suggests:` / `Codex counters:`
The settled table is shown before any individual question

behavior.setup: Same project; the user's registry has models enrolled but NO assignment for `adversary`.
behavior.prompt: /supermodo:grill add a --dry-run flag to the import command
assert: Exactly ONE approval table is shown, with a row per unapproved class and a closed menu approve all / change rows / decline
No planner is dispatched before the approval is persisted via `models.ts approve`
Declining leaves the grill not started — no self-adversary, no 'single-model' wording anywhere

behavior.setup: Registry: only one lineage approved for both lead and adversary (e.g. two Codex models).
behavior.prompt: /supermodo:grill add a --dry-run flag to the import command
assert: The skill reports the unstaffed seat by id with the broker's reason (shares lineage …)
It offers exactly: staff it / run a fully staffed variant / abort
It does not start the grill in any degraded form

behavior.setup: A planner dispatch returns status failed (identity mismatch).
assert: The grill stops and reports seat, requested pin and cause
No other model is substituted for the failed seat
The report states verification/independence as not reached
